sentences.text: Brachygnathosuchus is an extinct genus of crocodilian known for its unusually broad and stout lower jaw. The name literally translates to "short jawed crocodile," highlighting this distinctive feature.

The dentary bone, which forms the lower jaw, differs significantly from other crocodilians and was initially mistaken for a dinosaur bone. An associated eroded osteoderm, a type of bony skin shield, confirms its classification within the crocodilian lineage.
Fossils of this animal were discovered in the Upper Purus River in western Brazil and were formally described by Mook in 1921.
Because the fossils were found in riverbed silt without lithified strata, scientists cannot date them with certainty.
Taxonomically, Brachygnathosuchus belongs to the parent group Crocodylia and is classified in the class Reptilia.
Associated fossils suggest Brachygnathosuchus lived during the Pliocene, specifically between 11.63 and 7.246 million years ago during the Tortonian.
